architecture.approach: Four lifecycle templates live in one server-side registry that renders subject plus HTML/text from a fully escaped context. Dispatch goes through an idempotent record-then-send action: the key (registrationId + template) is written before the provider call, so a repeated cron sweep or a retry finds it and returns early. Two cron sweeps enqueue reminders and follow-ups; the registration mutation only schedules the confirmation, so provider latency never reaches the mutation. A single preference check in the dispatch path suppresses optional email, while the confirmation template is marked transactional and bypasses it.

components.description: Template registry (confirmation, reminder_24h, post_event_thankyou, feedback_request) plus the escaping renderer and the idempotency key builder.

components.name: convex/lifecycleDispatch.ts
components.description: Idempotent dispatch: record the key, honour the preference for optional templates, send through Mailtrap, record the outcome, retry within a bounded budget.

components.name: convex/emailLog.ts
components.description: Record lifecycle templates with registrationId and idempotencyKey, and expose the per-registration delivery rows.

components.description: Extend emailEvents.template with the four lifecycle values and add registrationId/idempotencyKey; add registrations.emailOptOut.

components.name: convex/crons.ts
components.description: Hourly reminder sweep (events starting in 24 plus or minus 1 hours) and follow-up sweep (events ended), both idempotent.

fields.name: template
fields.type: union(invite, announcement, registration_confirmation, reminder_24h, post_event_thankyou, feedback_request)

dataModel.flowDescription: A registration triggers an internal scheduling call; the dispatch action writes an emailEvents row keyed by registrationId + template before contacting Mailtrap, then updates that row to sent or failed. The two cron sweeps call internal queries that only return registrations without a row for the template in question, so repeats are no-ops. Cancellation stops future reminders because the sweeps filter on confirmed status.

securityConsiderations.description: One send per recipient: the dispatch action takes a single registration and derives the recipient from it; no BCC and no caller-supplied address.
The renderer escapes every interpolated value and receives only that registration's context, so cross-recipient data cannot enter a body.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The registration mutation schedules and returns; the provider call happens in a separate action, so provider latency and outages never reach the mutation.
Retries use a bounded attempt counter stored on the emailEvents row; the sweep skips rows at the limit and leaves them visible as failed.
The reminder sweep is batched per run and keyed on an indexed time window so a large event does not produce an unbounded scan.

dependencies.name: Mailtrap transport
dependencies.notes: convex/mailtrap.ts supplies endpoint selection, payload building and the sandbox switch; lifecycle email reuses it unchanged.

dependencies.name: Cron infrastructure
dependencies.notes: convex/crons.ts and cronRuns already record scheduled runs.

risks.description: A cron restart double-sends a reminder.
risks.mitigation: Idempotency key is written before dispatch; the sweep only selects registrations with no row for that template.

risks.description: Email latency or an outage blocks registration.
risks.mitigation: Scheduling only; the action runs afterwards and failures are recorded rather than thrown.

risks.description: Opt-out is honoured inconsistently across templates.
risks.mitigation: One preference check in the dispatch path, with the transactional flag on the confirmation template.
